notes: Example declaration for `chowder growth campaign run`. Identity is two objects: `base_model_path`/`base_model_digest` name the dense base, and `parent_adapter_path`/`parent_adapter_digest` name the parent generation's adapter over it (omit both when the parent *is* the base). Each digest is verified against its own tree before compute; a base digest is never accepted as an adapter digest. Every path above is relative to the repository root and must exist before a run; the runner refuses a declared-but-missing input by name. `recipes` must be exactly the ids `chowder growth campaign plan <this file>` prints -- the planner owns recipe identity, and a run refuses an id the planner did not propose. The two ids here are placeholders and deliberately do not match, so `plan` reports "recipes_declared": false. `device_time_measured: false` is the honest setting for the current trainer, which charges wall time: the device ceilings then bound the *projected plan* (per recipe and for the campaign as a whole) and the run records that they were not settled against measured device time. `protection` declares the branch-protection policy certification applies *before* any lineage record: the trusted ancestor (`gen0`), the regression tolerance, and the mini-slice protocol a protected row must match. `baseline_eval_report_path` is the arm those slices are compared against. The candidate arm is deliberately absent from this list: it is a run *output*, produced by evaluating the adapter the run trained and selected (the run requires an evaluation seam and refuses without one), and a report prepared outside the run is no longer an accepted input. `evaluation_material_path` is the other half of that sentence: the report is an output, but the *data* it is measured on is an input, so the campaign declares one dataset per declared benchmark and the production evaluator measures exactly those items. Its shape is `{"suites": [{"benchmark_qualified_id": "math500@2024-04", "name": "math500", "dataset": "<jsonl path>", "scoring": "normalized_exact_match", "metric": "accuracy"}]}`: one suite per declared benchmark id, each naming a JSONL file whose items carry the scoring fields. The evaluator writes the first `protection.n_samples` items of each dataset, in dataset order, into the run root as the slice it measures, so a dataset shorter than the declared protocol refuses before any model load. A campaign that declares no protection policy, or whose candidate evaluation does not name the artifact the run selected, refuses or reaches INCONCLUSIVE and records no promoted generation.
